The accepted incumbent (attempt 002) already implements the fixed source recurrence with the minimum possible work, and the remaining candidate space is either forbidden by the fixed-source contract or pure noise. Evidence and reasoning: (1) Business trace required by the CURRENT equations: deq2list emptyq lst = lst; deq2list (v#va) lst = (let (x,xq) = dequeue (v#va) in deq2list xq (x#lst)). Since dequeue = (last, butlast) and the recursive call is in tail position, each source step is exactly one final-element split of q plus one cons onto the front of acc, and the final value is q ++ acc. The incumbent's `while let Some(x) = q.pop_back() { acc.push_front(x) }` performs exactly one pop_back (the last/butlast split) and one push_front (the cons) per logical element, in that order, with the same accumulator dependency and no reordering — verified against the actual loop body, not the comments. (2) Memory-traffic floor: any realization that keeps all n visits must read each of the n elements once from q's storage and write it once into acc's storage. The incumbent does exactly 1 alloc (acc.reserve(q.len()) then a single reserved-capacity buffer), n reads, n writes, and no extra passes. I evaluated the only alternative storage spellings the contract permits: (a) push into a reversed staging buffer then one final decode — the decode adds an extra n/2-swap (or n extra moves) pass, strictly more traffic; (b) maintain acc in reversed form (cons = push_back) — requires an extra reverse(acc) upfront plus a final full reverse, adding n/2+m swaps; (c) VecDeque::drain(..).rev() with for_each push_front — same n moves, only replaces one predictable Option branch, i.e. noise, and attempt 003 already measured the same class of micro-variation at geomean 1.003 with a 0.976 workload (rejected, conservative_lower 0.971). (3) The only structurally large remaining win — returning q unchanged (or appending acc into q's buffer) when acc is empty / skipping per-element visits — changes the recurrence by removing logical dequeues and conses; it is not a pure storage encoding of the same transitions, so it requires a proved source transformation, which this rust-only stage forbids (stage_contract.source_recurrence_change_allowed = false). Feasibility of a source direction is also poor: the source already equals q ++ acc, so a proof would collapse the recurrence rather than reduce constant factors, and that is outside the current stage. (4) Numeric/representation obligations are unaffected: no i2r_numeric operations exist on this path, List<T>/VecDeque<T> and Prod<A,B> stay generic with no Clone/Copy bound, dequeue still panics on the source-undefined empty input, and no public signature changes. Measured position: 4.59x geomean over the baseline with per-workload medians 168 ns / 613 ns / 2529 ns (descending-64, duplicates-256, descending-1024), i.e. ~2.4 ns/element on a serialized pointer/len update chain; the residue is allocation plus unavoidable two-stream element movement, not removable work. Therefore no further Rust refinement has a plausible measured gain, and further attempts would spend the shared budget on noise-level variants (two such attempts would also risk the three-consecutive-unsuccessful stop).

Removing those buffers would need either a shared/recycled scratch representation threaded through the frozen `pub fn merge<A: Ord>(List<A>, List<A>) -> List<A>` / `pub fn msort<A: Ord>(List<A>) -> List<A>` interfaces, or an in-place/rotation merge (unsafe or a different comparison/emission sequence), both of which are forbidden here: the stage contract fixes the source recurrence, no unsafe is permitted, and a changed visitation/comparison schedule would require a proved source transformation that this rust-only stage cannot submit. The declared native boundaries also pin `size_list`, `divide_nat`, `nat_of_num` and `less_eq` to their exact primitives, so replacing the Nat size/division with a machine shift, hoisting/caching the numeral 2 across calls, or skipping the split/size computations for favourable inputs are all excluded (and would be benchmark-shaped shortcuts rather than source-supported work reductions). Removing any of these additions or the always-evaluated +2 guard, replacing max+1, or substituting a strided/closed-form height or visitation schedule would change the CURRENT source recurrence and is a source-stage change, which this stage forbids.
2) node_b (7167 calls, ~0.80 ms exclusive) performs exactly one allocation per constructed node plus the required node_height computation; identity subtrees are already returned in place (insert EQ returns the original box, delete on Leaf returns the leaf box, delete EQ with a leaf left child returns the right box, split_max base case returns the left box), so no redundant per-level free/reallocate remains.
